text: Thought suppression involves active attempts to inhibit unwanted thoughts which may provoke negative emotions [ 26 , 27 ]. Thought suppression has been linked to increased rates of depression [ 28 ]. However, longitudinal studies suggest that thought suppression may interact with life stress, predicting higher rates of depression under conditions of high stress only [ 29 ]. Studies of the general population indicate that attempts to suppress thoughts typically result in a heightened accessibility of suppressed thoughts (e.g., a rebound effect) together with increases in emotional and physiological arousal [ 27 ].
source_label: Attachment style, thought suppression, self-compassion and depression: Testing a serial mediation model
